title: Calderano and Diaz win singles titles as Americas Championships spread the honours
standfirst: Hugo Calderano beat fellow Brazilian Guilherme Teodoro in Lima, Adriana Diaz beat Canada's Mo Zhang, and no country won more than two titles.

image.alt: Hugo Calderano playing at the 2019 Pan American Games in Lima
image.caption: Calderano in Lima, 2019

body: Hugo Calderano won the men's singles at the ITTF-Americas Championships in Lima, beating his Brazilian team-mate Guilherme Teodoro 4-1 in the final. Puerto Rico's Adriana Diaz took the women's title, beating Canada's Mo Zhang 4-2.

Calderano is ranked seventh in the world and the only player from the Americas in the men's top 10, so the singles title was expected. The rest of the week was far less predictable, with titles shared between Brazil, Puerto Rico, Canada, Chile and the United States.
The USA's women were the most dominant team. They beat Guatemala 3-0 and Canada 3-1, then Puerto Rico 3-0 in the final, according to Butterfly's report.

Chile's Nicolas Burgos and Gustavo Gomez won the men's doubles, beating Venezuela's Medina and Rios 3-0. Brazil's Giulia Takahashi and Laura Watanabe took the women's doubles with a 3-0 win over the American pair Sally Moyland and Lily Zhang.
Mo Zhang left Lima with a title after all. She and Edward Ly won the mixed doubles for Canada, beating Teodoro and Takahashi 3-0, which also denied Teodoro a second title.
Reports of the men's team final differed: Butterfly's headline credits Venezuela, while its match report names Argentina as beating Brazil 3-2. Eleven will update this when results are confirmed.
The WTT tour now moves to Europe, with Champions events in Montpellier and Frankfurt over the next fortnight.
